parsed.rationale: All five records share `kind: type-alias-object`, reside in the same package (`MusicShareKit`) under `Shared/MusicShareKit/Sources/MusicShareKit/Services/`, carry empty `fields_or_signature` lists, and have `shared_field_count: 1` — indicating the pipeline found exactly one shared structural slot (the alias declaration itself). Because the aliased types are not surfaced in the cluster data, it is impossible to determine whether the five aliases resolve to the same concrete type (in which case four of the five files are redundant) or to five distinct types that happen to share alias-declaration shape (in which case a generic or protocol abstraction is warranted). No restraint markers are present, so intentional-duplication rules do not apply, but the evidence is insufficient to commit to a specific refactor category without inspecting the alias targets.

specifics.proposed_action: Investigate whether the five type-alias-objects (AppleMusicService, BandcampService, SoundCloudService, SpotifyService, YouTubeMusicService) in MusicShareKit/Services/ are all aliasing the same underlying type. If so, introduce a single generic or parameterised service type (e.g., a generic struct `MusicService<Platform>` where `Platform` is a new enum or phantom type enumerating the five platforms) and replace all five files with that one declaration. If the aliases are aliasing different underlying types that merely share structural shape at the alias-declaration site, consider whether a shared protocol (e.g., `MusicServiceProtocol`) with a macro or enum-driven factory would reduce the per-file boilerplate.
specifics.why_no_category_fits: The cluster records are all `kind: type-alias-object` with empty `fields_or_signature` lists, meaning the structural pipeline detected identical shape at the alias declaration site but provides no information about what each alias resolves to. Without knowing the aliased types, `extract-to-common` does not apply (there is nothing to move — aliases are not implementations), `generic-parameterization` cannot be fully specified (the constraint on the type parameter is unknown), and `macro-synthesis` is premature. The most honest recommendation is to inspect the aliased targets first, then choose between generic-parameterization or a protocol-based approach. Neither fits cleanly given the available evidence.
